hyps.why: With edge 5 removed, edge 3 carries more of the output, so adding a 3x3 conv there matters more.
Removing edge 3 when edge 5 is already none leaves only edge 4 or no path to the output, which severely hurts accuracy.
When edge 4 is none, node 1 reaches the output only indirectly through edge 2 or not at all, so improving edge 0 matters less.
If edge 5 is none, node 2's output is discarded, so changing edge 1 has little effect.
If edge 5 is none, node 2 has no outgoing edge, so a conv on edge 2 is wasted.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 receives nothing, so edge 4 only passes zeros.
Removing edge 5 when edge 3 is none leaves only edge 4 or no path to the output, which is far more harmful than when the direct edge exists.
With edge 5 none, removing edge 4 leaves only the direct edge 3 to the output, which costs depth and capacity.
With edge 1 also none, removing edge 0 leaves nodes 1 and 2 empty, so the cell reduces to edge 3 alone.
Replacing a parameter-free pooling op on the direct input-to-output edge with a conv adds capacity, so the gain is larger than when replacing other ops.
